# the contributor audit: complete ear derivatives and a quadrilateral neighborhood



Sources:

* `candidate 8e1d01c76d1a2560`
* `candidate 3be9fc800740b04a`

The unique-tip source differentiates the actual positive cap/section data at a tight strict-incidence triangle. Its differential coefficients retain both the denominator M and the total area. The unique-sector coefficients alpha_i are strictly positive by the displayed square identities and 0<r<2. The edge coordinates have fixed Jacobian, so integration of the actual triangular tent gives the volume derivatives; the section derivative follows by intersecting the moving cutting line with that tent. It remains valid when the peak is exactly on a cutting ray. The affine endpoint tents have zero cost because they are actual two-sided triangle variations at a maximum, not because an arbitrary shape derivative is assumed stationary. Subtraction yields the negative unique-tip costs with their exact endpoint factors. This completes the fixed-peak ear directions omitted from the earlier double-sector sources, while correctly leaving the vanishing endpoint derivative separate.

The neighborhood source supplies the missing uniform control for one-point ears. Its exact clipping formulas have matching branches at a zero tip margin, positive denominators uniformly near the fixed strict triangle, and bounded one-sided derivatives. Thus the cap and section data have a common O(eta^2) remainder; the smooth positive-data row functional inherits it. Compactness is used only after that uniform estimate. Away from vertices, all fixed-peak derivatives are uniformly negative, including transition peaks.

At a vertex-concentrated peak, the identities R=(1+a)A-aC, a=eta/[1-(1+eta)theta], and Q=(1-b)R+bB are exact. They express the actual quadrilateral as a nearby triangle minus exactly one corner. The area loss E=k eta(1+eta)theta/[1-(1+eta)theta] is correct. All three corner vertices remain in one strict sign sector for one uniform neighborhood, with no lower bound on theta/eta. Hence the actual sections remain fixed and exactly one cap and total area lose E. The previously audited corner derivative is negative continuously in this nearby triangle data, establishing the finite sign even when the ear derivative tends to zero. The corner cut need not be parallel to its opposite side; only its sign-sector containment is used in the exact data formula.

Every sufficiently close genuine quadrilateral has three distinct extremal vertices near the old vertices, by the barycentric coordinate estimate. The fourth vertex has one negative and two positive barycentric coordinates relative to those three, because all four are extreme and their diagonals cross internally. It is therefore the stated one-edge ear. The support-function inclusions bound eta uniformly and preserve the source interior. Dilation about the source gives the cap and chord continuity used for initially strict rows.

The theorem is genuinely uniform among triangles and quadrilaterals. It does not establish a neighborhood among arbitrary polygons, and does not preserve any adjacent mixed fibers. A simultaneous many-ear or convex-body reduction is still required before applying it outside this scope.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
